name: Gaoyuzhuang seaweeds
size: Ribbons up to about 30 cm long
fact: Long, flat ribbons up to 30 cm long and 8 cm wide, 1.56 billion years old — the oldest living things big enough to see with your own eyes. Their regular shapes and cells show they were many-celled seaweeds.

name: Rafatazmia
fact: Tiny threads of cells in 1.6-billion-year-old rocks in India, with walls and structures inside that look like those of red seaweeds. If they are red algae, they are the oldest.
debate: Bacteria can make threads that look like this, and the structures inside the cells are hard to read. Many scientists think it is too old to be a red alga.

name: Tappania
fact: A single cell with branching arms growing out of its wall — a complex cell with a nucleus, perhaps an early fungus or alga. Its shape could change as it grew, which bacteria cannot do.
